solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Infatuated with bustle and girdle

parts.note: bustle, a fuss or commotion, gives ADO
to girdle is to encircle, and a ring is a band that encircles

explanation.surface: Someone besotted with an old-fashioned dress's bustle and girdle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being infatuated with someone means worshipping or idolising them, the participle sense of doting.

clue.text: Bowman fiddling in orchestra not drunken sot

indicators.note: fiddling means messing about with, so the letters of orchestra are rearranged
not says some letters are left out of the mix, and drunken says those letters, from sot, come out in any order

explanation.surface: A violinist playing in an orchestra who is not a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: rearrange the letters of ORCHESTRA once S, O and T have been taken out, leaving RCHERA. 'fiddling' and 'not drunken' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman is one who shoots with a bow and arrow, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Old baronet to employ Angle

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: An elderly baronet hiring a man called Angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an obtuse angle is one type of angle, so the word names a kind of angle rather than meaning 'angle' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle between ninety and one hundred and eighty degrees is described by this adjective, so it stands for a type of angle.

clue.text: Weak bishop that is free without

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the letters for that is and free go around the bishop

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
solute is an old word for free or loose, unattached

explanation.surface: A feeble churchman who would be free if he had nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, an old sense. RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title; SOLUTE is a rare word for free.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak person in this sense lacks firmness of purpose and cannot make up their mind.

clue.text: Good headgear found where 24 takes place

parts.note: hats are headgear

explanation.surface: Smart headwear spotted at the site of some ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 24 is SATI, the old Hindu practice of a widow burning herself on her husband's pyre; such pyres stood on the river steps of India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India these are the riverside steps where cremations happen, the scene of a widow's self-immolation.

clue.text: Appropriate objective for 8

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it
an objective is an aim

explanation.surface: A suitable goal for the people at answer 8.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to seize. The definition is what the marksmen of 8 do before shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpshooters line up their sights on a target before firing, which is the action the phrase names.

clue.text: Rage and it could become his profession

definitions.text: Rage and it could become his profession

indicators.note: could become says these letters can be turned into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Fury could be the career of an actor who rants on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: raging on stage is the job of a tragic actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragic actor rants and storms through plays like Lear, so rage is in effect his trade.

clue.text: Chief of a thousand Chinese

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
the Han are the main ethnic group of China

explanation.surface: The leader of a thousand people in China.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the title of a ruler or chieftain among Mongols and Central Asian peoples.

clue.text: Dictator taking vehicle about desert

parts.note: an auto is a car
C stands for circa, about
to rat is to desert, like a rat leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A tyrant driving his car around the Sahara.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler holding absolute power is a dictator, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Evangelist's soldiers: they 5 across

parts.note: St Mark is one of the four Evangelists, the gospel writers
men is a common word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops belonging to a gospel writer, all lining up their shots.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 5 across is TAKE AIM, so the definition is 'they take aim'.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert shooters are the people who line up their sights at a target.

clue.text: Jazz fan starts to employ Reinhardt to provide entertainment

parts.note: a cat is old jazz slang for a fan or player

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of employ and Reinhardt are used

explanation.surface: A jazz lover begins to hire guitarist Django Reinhardt to put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Django Reinhardt was a famous jazz guitarist, which makes 'Jazz fan' read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or amusement for an event, as in catering for guests.

clue.text: Altar base could well be made of this

definitions.text: Altar base could well be made of this

indicators.note: could well be made says the letters of altar base can be made into something new

explanation.surface: A remark about what an altar's foundation might be built from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: altars are often of this white stone.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine white stone, a form of gypsum, is often carved for church fittings and altars.

clue.text: Bright ones mostly to be found here (with initial rejects!)

definitions.text: Bright ones mostly to be found here (with initial rejects!)

parts.words: Bright ones mostly to be found here (with initial rejects!)
parts.note: bright ones with most of the last word gives Brighton, the seaside town, and the county holding it is the place where it is found

explanation.surface: Clever people are mostly found in one place, apart from a few cast-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut 'Bright ones' short and it becomes Brighton, a seaside city on the English south coast, which lies in this county.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is in this south-coast county of England, so it is where the town is found.

clue.text: Book of deeds

definitions.meaning: a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A ledger recording things that were done.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth New Testament book has this short name, and the word also means actions or feats.

clue.text: No time for a romance at a party for amateur

indicators.note: no time says the letter for time, T, is removed

parts.note: a romance is a novel, a piece of fiction
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone too busy for a love affair at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amateur' is used in its root sense of a lover of something, an enthusiast, not a non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast or devoted fan of an activity, which is what amateur once meant: a lover of it.

clue.text: Having crushed my pomace fill fire in bowl

indicators.note: crushed means pressed and broken up, so the letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Having pressed my grape pulp, fill the bowl and light a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Pomace is the pulp left after pressing fruit for wine or cider.
explanation.definitionFit: At the Games a torch-lit fire burns in a great cauldron or bowl throughout the event.

clue.text: Islander finds gold in shaken Martini

indicators.note: in places the gold symbol inside the shaken letters
shaken, as a cocktail is, says the letters of Martini are mixed up

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone on an island discovers gold in a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' turns MARTINI into MRITIAN-style letters; 'in' puts AU among them to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Mauritius, an island nation in the Indian Ocean, is an islander.

clue.text: Pillars of damaged silks to follow order

indicators.note: to follow says the damaged silks come after the order

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an order of chivalry

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of silks are spoiled into a different order

explanation.surface: Columns of ruined silk that must obey a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall tapering stone columns, like Cleopatra's Needle, are pillars of a kind.

clue.text: In SW Pacific state Victor earns rupees for urns

indicators.note: in places Victor inside the Pacific state

parts.note: Samoa is an island state in the south-west Pacific
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: In a Pacific island nation, a man named Victor earns money in Indian currency to buy urns.
explanation.definitionFit: These Russian metal tea urns hold and heat water for brewing tea.

clue.text: Black coat worn by most recent new champion smelt here

indicators.note: worn by puts the coat after the most recent, as clothing on a wearer

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
last means most recent, as in last week
fur is an animal's coat
an ace is a champion, an expert

explanation.surface: A fur coat on the newest champion, who smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smelt' looks like the past tense of smell, but it is the verb for extracting metal from ore by heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron ore is smelted in this huge furnace with a forced air draught.

clue.text: Fix one on small cog

parts.note: to pin is to fix in place
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Attach one item onto a little gear wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinion is the smaller gear wheel that meshes with a larger one in a train of gears.

clue.text: Old kingdom, new Earl

definitions.meaning: the ancient Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the West Saxons in southern England
Prince Edward was created Earl of this title in 1999, a then new earldom

explanation.surface: A former realm gets a newly made nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The earldom was revived in 1999 for Prince Edward, the Queen's youngest son, so it was new when the clue was set.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Anglo-Saxon realm of Alfred the Great and is also the title of a royal earldom.

clue.text: Celebrity left on one leg

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A famous person balancing on one leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, the half of the field behind a right-hander's legs, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary or social lion is a much-sought-after celebrity, as in being lionised.

clue.text: Promiscuously erotic Li Po shielded people maintaining order

indicators.note: promiscuously means indiscriminately, in a random jumble, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The Chinese poet Li Po, wildly amorous, needed protection from the forces of order.
explanation.walkthrough: Li Po was a classical Chinese poet famous for his love of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers who control unruly crowds carry shields, so they are shielded keepers of public order.

clue.text: Actor on Thursday has sixth sense

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the so-called sixth sense

explanation.surface: A performer who has a premonition on Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: This is informal shortening of thespian, a performer on the stage, after Thespis of ancient Greece.

clue.text: It's a terrible way to go

definitions.text: It's a terrible way to go

parts.words: It's a terrible way to go
parts.note: a way to go means a way to die here, and the former Hindu custom of a widow burning on her husband's pyre is a dreadful death

explanation.surface: A grim remark about a dreadful route or a ghastly death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to go' suggests a route, but it means a way of dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The banned practice of a widow being burned alive with her late husband is a horrific death.

clue.text: Spice Girl in sin bin regularly starts to seek escape

indicators.note: in places the girl among the letters picked from sin bin
regularly says every other letter of sin bin is used

parts.note: Tara is a girl's name

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of seek and escape are taken

explanation.surface: One of the Spice Girls is sent to the penalty box and keeps trying to break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes S, N, I from 'sin bin'; TARA goes inside after the S. A sin bin is where a penalised rugby or hockey player sits out.
explanation.definitionFit: This star-shaped Chinese seed pod is a spice with an aniseed flavour.

clue.text: Ram airliners regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of airliners, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A command to crash planes into each other on a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ram' looks like a verb, but it is the zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sign of the zodiac is symbolised by a ram.

clue.text: Property river's swept away in time spent drinking

indicators.note: swept away says the river is removed, as if carried off by a current

parts.note: property is a possession, something owned
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Land lost when a river floods, then a long spell at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking session is a period given over to drinking, as in a long session at the pub.

clue.text: Legendary bird found in American state capital

definitions.meaning: the mythical bird that rises reborn from its own ashes

explanation.surface: A mythical creature spotted in a US capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled firebird reborn from ashes shares its name with the capital of Arizona.
